headline: SOUTH32 DUMPS $5.6B ALUMINUM EMPIRE TO ALCOA ON NEW CEO'S FIRST DAY — PIVOTS TO COPPER, ZINC, SILVER
snippet: South32 Ltd (ASX:S32) agreed on June 30 — new CEO Matthew Daley's first day in office — to sell nearly its entire aluminium portfolio to Alcoa Corporation for up to US$5.6 billion: US$3.1 billion in cash, approximately US$1 billion in Alcoa shares, and a US$750 million contingent value right tied to future alumina and aluminium prices. The deal strips South32 of Worsley Alumina (86%), Hillside Aluminium in South Africa (100%), and three Brazilian assets, repositioning the company as a focused copper, zinc, silver, and lead miner — a direct bet on electrification demand while offloading its most carbon-intensive, lowest-margin operations.

headline: SILVER AT $57 — DOWN 52% FROM JANUARY'S $121 PEAK: 6TH STRAIGHT DEFICIT YEAR FAILS TO SUPPORT PRICE
snippet: Silver spot fell to approximately US$57–58 per ounce on July 1, 2026 — roughly half the US$121 peak reached in January and down nearly 20% year-to-date — as hawkish Federal Reserve repricing, dollar strength, and mass liquidation of speculative positions reversed what had been the metal's largest-ever bull run. The disconnect is stark: the Silver Institute's World Silver Survey 2026 projected a sixth consecutive year of structural supply deficit totalling a record 215 million ounces, yet paper-market selling has erased those fundamentals — drawing debate over whether the futures-led price action can hold against rising Asian physical demand near current levels.

headline: ST GEORGE MINING DRILLS 199.5M OF RARE EARTHS FROM SURFACE AT ARAXÁ — BEST HOLE IN PROJECT HISTORY (ASX:SGQ)
snippet: St George Mining (ASX:SGQ) delivered its thickest-ever diamond drill intercept at the 100%-owned Araxá Rare Earths and Niobium Project in Minas Gerais, Brazil: hole AXDD120 cut 199.5 metres of continuous mineralisation from surface at 2.86% total rare earth oxides (TREO) and 0.44% niobium oxide (Nb₂O₅), including 60 metres at 3.96% TREO from surface. The result — released approximately 15 hours ago — reaffirms open-pit potential for the large carbonatite system and follows a A$60 million capital raise anchored by Hancock Prospecting, positioning Araxá as one of the world's highest-grade development-stage rare earth and niobium projects outside China.

headline: 37.55 g/t AuEq OVER 27M AT 300M DEPTH: COLLECTIVE MINING HITS TUNGSTEN-GOLD SUBZONE BELOW APOLLO (TSX:CNL)
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX:CNL / NYSE:CNL) reported a new discovery at the Apollo system of its Guayabales Project in Caldas, Colombia: hole APC-162 intersected 27.35 metres at 37.55 g/t gold equivalent (1.68% WO₃, 11.62 g/t Au, 54 g/t Ag, 0.43% Cu) from 300 metres below surface, opening a distinct tungsten-enriched high-grade subzone well below the known near-surface tungsten zone. With 13 drill rigs operating, US$113.3 million in cash (as of March 31), and 120,000 metres completed at Apollo alone, the company is funded to immediately follow up what may be a new high-grade corridor at depth — distinct from any previously modelled mineralisation.

headline: Li-FT POWER DRILLS 26M AT 1.29% Li2O AT BIG EAST — FIRST HOLES IN YELLOWKNIFE AREA SINCE 2024 RESOURCE (TSXV:LIFT)
snippet: Li-FT Power Ltd (TSXV:LIFT / ASX:LFT) released results from the 2026 winter program at the Yellowknife Lithium Project (YLP) in the Northwest Territories, with 17 new holes (4,778 metres) at the BIG area returning highlights of YLP-0312 at 26 metres of 1.29% Li₂O (including 17 metres at 1.65% Li₂O) — the first drilling at BIG since the October 2024 inferred resource estimate was published. YLP's consolidated inferred resource stands at 50.4 million tonnes at 1.00% Li₂O (506,000 tonnes Li₂O contained), making it one of the largest spodumene projects in North America; all 17 new holes intersected lithium-bearing pegmatite.

headline: GOLD $4,028, SILVER $58.63 HOLD KEY SUPPORT — JUNE PAYROLLS AND JULY 4 HOLIDAY KEEP METALS IN LIMBO
snippet: Gold spot held near US$4,028 per ounce and silver near US$58.63 on July 1 as both metals bounced from short-covering near major support levels while a firmer US dollar and elevated Treasury yields capped any meaningful recovery ahead of Thursday's June Non-Farm Payrolls report. Analysts noted that thin pre-holiday liquidity ahead of the July 4 Independence Day weekend could amplify the payrolls reaction in either direction: a stronger-than-expected jobs number risks triggering another leg down by reinforcing September rate-hike pricing near 65%, while a miss could provide the circuit breaker that gold bulls have been waiting for since the death cross formed in late June.

headline: APEX CRITICAL METALS DRILLS BC CARBONATITE MAGNETIC ANOMALY — 2026 PROGRAM TARGETS NIOBIUM AND REE AT DEPTH (CSE:APXC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Apex Critical Metals
snippet: Apex Critical Metals Corp (CSE:APXC) mobilized a diamond drill rig to its Cap Critical Minerals Project (85 km northeast of Prince George, BC) to begin a four-hole, approximately 1,200-metre program with two objectives: drill the core of a previously untested magnetic anomaly that may reflect a deep carbonatite body prospective for niobium and rare earth mineralisation, and extend the 2025 niobium discovery where hole CAP25-006 returned 124.5 metres at 0.27% Nb₂O₅ — including 10 metres at 1.08% Nb₂O₅. The program is fully permitted under the company's Multi-Year Area-Based permit, positioning Cap as an early-stage Canadian niobium discovery at a time when the West is scrambling to de-risk rare metal supply chains from China.

headline: GOLD'S SUMMER DOLDRUMS ARE HERE — ANALYSTS SAY SEASONAL TROUGH OPENS BEST BUYING WINDOW FOR MINERS IN 18 MONTHS
snippet: GoldSeek's seasonal analysis of gold and miners argues that July 2026 marks the onset of gold's weakest calendar window — the summer doldrums — but that the depth of the current sell-off from January's US$5,600 per ounce high makes the setup more bullish than usual: GDX has fallen below its 200-day moving average for the first time in 16.6 months, reaching its least technically extended level since before the 218.9% advance that ended in late February 2026. Historical data from 2001–2025 shows mid-July to late September as the seasonal accumulation window, with gold averaging 5.5% gains into late September across those years before the stronger Q4 move typically begins.

headline: 5.4 g/t AU IN QUEBEC SURFACE ROCK: BULLION GOLD STARTS VALIDATION DRILL AT TERRAGOLD SHOWING (TSXV:BGD)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Bullion Gold Resources
snippet: Bullion Gold Resources Corp (TSXV:BGD) reported four surface grab samples from the Terragold Gold Project in the Senneterre area of Quebec, including a best result of 5.4 g/t Au and 5.0 g/t Ag from the historical Terragold Showing, and commenced validation drilling funded by a recently closed C$2 million private placement. The company is targeting historical high-grade gold intercepts across a multi-kilometre auriferous corridor in the Abitibi belt; structural and lithological mapping completed ahead of drilling has confirmed controls on the mineralisation consistent with the regional gold-bearing shear zone that hosts multiple producing mines in the broader district.

headline: CHINA OPENS YUAN LITHIUM FUTURES TO OVERSEAS TRADERS JULY 3 — GFEX CREATES GLOBAL PRICE BENCHMARK
snippet: China's Guangzhou Futures Exchange (GFEX) confirmed that its yuan-denominated lithium carbonate futures and options will be open to overseas investors and traders from July 3, 2026, granting global participants direct access to the world's largest and most liquid lithium futures market — GFEX recorded 6.3 million lots of lithium carbonate volume in May alone versus just 1,051 lots on the CME. Overseas traders may post US dollars as margin subject to a 5% haircut; analysts view the internationalisation as part of Beijing's push to establish the yuan as the global pricing currency for battery materials, with direct implications for how juniors and producers price offtake agreements and how institutional investors hedge lithium exposure.
